The fix items PI-20260929-K85Q64SF-0001..0004 have sat QUEUED since 2026-09-29 (dropped work). (3) The package 'confidence' field is a constant 1.0 on 61 of 200 packages (strategy default, not a model output) and the UI must not present it as an ML confidence. (4) ml_entry packages (5 of 200) carry no modelScores at all, although ml_entry is itself a model whose probability is the natural confidence. (5) /api/bot/positions carries no strategy and no scores (the UI must join the order package). PLAN (after the 2026-11-11 reset): a. serve the missing features in the shadow scorer (or retrain conviction on the features live can serve), re-shadow, verify every new package gets a score; b. write ml_entry's own probability as its confidence; c. render the 1.0 default as '—'; d. walk-forward backfill: for each closed trade, score it with a model trained ONLY on trades closed before its entry (no in-sample scores; the corpus is ~hundreds of trades, so state n), then calibration / hit-rate vs outcome by decile, net of cost; e. show the score in the trade cards (UI-REDESIGN-2026-11). OPERATOR DECISION 2026-11-09 ~11:20Z: build a SEPARATE confidence-scoring model, independent of the entry models (ml_entry's own probability is recorded too, but does not replace it); design it around the inputs it actually needs (likely more than today's 10, so a redesign), feed it those inputs live, and make it a TOP ML priority for the week after the 2026-11-11 reset. PLAN v1 (manager): (1) DESIGN: target = net-of-cost trade outcome (won / R multiple) for ANY strategy's order package at entry; inputs = strategy-agnostic package context (strategy id, direction, R:R, stop distance in ATR, time/session), market state at entry (vol regime, trend/ADX, funding/basis/OI where the symbol has them, book_depth once 98e3-36 lands), the entry model's own score when one exists, and account/book context; every input must be servable at entry time from the live path (no train/serve skew - the JC-SA-02 failure). (2) PARITY FIRST: one feature builder shared by training and the live scorer, plus a CI parity test that fails if a declared feature is not served. (3) DATA: label corpus = every closed trade across books (state n per book), plus walk-forward replayed trades from the backtest corpus to get past the ~hundreds of live labels. (4) VALIDATION: walk-forward (train only on trades before each scored trade), calibration by decile, discrimination (AUC), and the money test registered before the run: does filtering or sizing by the score improve net P&L on held-out trades vs no filter. (5) LIVE: shadow-score every new package from day one (score shown in the trade cards and the review), promotion to advisory only on the registered test. (6) BACKFILL: walk-forward scores for every past trade, stored with the trade, compared to its outcome. Owner: the one ML lane, first item after the reset. OPERATOR ADDENDUM 2026-11-09 ~12:30Z: (A) LOG EVERY confidence score (the confidence model's entry score, every in-trade re-score, the entry model's own probability, the conviction field) with timestamp, model id+version, inputs hash, and link to the order package / trade / review_id, in one store the performance review reads. (B) The weekly /performance-review gains a fixed CONFIDENCE section: calibration (reliability by decile, Brier), discrimination (AUC), score-vs-realized-R by strategy/book, entry score vs later re-scores, and whether acting on the score would have helped net of cost; findings become rows/units. (C) The confidence model RE-ASSESSES EACH OPEN TRADE AT EVERY LIVE REVIEW, not only at entry: the LTR packet carries the current score + its change since entry, and the reviewer records it. TRAINING FORMAT for (C): samples are (trade, decision-time) pairs - entry plus each review/bar checkpoint - with state features as of that time (open R, peak R, giveback, bars held, distance to SL/TP in ATR, regime now) and the label measured FROM that point (P(TP before SL) / remaining R net of cost); walk-forward splits GROUPED BY TRADE (all checkpoints of one trade in the same fold) so no trade leaks across train/test; serve-time features built by the same shared builder as training, with the CI parity test. Backfill (D) scores every historical checkpoint the same way. OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-11-09 ~12:33Z: the logging + calibration scope is EVERY score, not just the confidence model: every ML model's output on a trade or package (entry models, the confidence model, shadow / advisory heads, regime / setup-quality / execution-quality / exit heads), every LTR review's judgement confidence and forecast (p_target, direction, horizon), and every desk review's score. One append-only score log (who scored: model id+version or review_id+session, what: package/trade/review, when, the score and its meaning, inputs hash), joined to the realized outcome. The weekly /performance-review CONFIDENCE section grades ALL of them: calibration and discrimination per scorer, LTR/desk forecast hit rates vs their stated confidence, and which scorers add information net of cost. Existing partial stores to fold in rather than duplicate: order_packages.modelScores, the trainer shadow log, comms/live_review/reviews.jsonl (+ the forecast-grade first-passage grades), desk decisions, comms/claude_strategy_scores.jsonl.
